title: credit-rollback-on-shard-replay-causing-temporary-negative-balance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Production reports show transient account balances dropping below zero for a subset of API keys after cross-region shard failover and subsequent replay. Symptoms suggest credits are being rolled back in duplicate during the shard replay/rehydration path, causing short-lived negative balances and spurious enforcement (throttles and denied requests). This ticket documents investigation, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, and a fix plan.
observed_behavior: After a shard reallocation event (region failover or operator-triggered move), some API keys briefly show negative credit balances. Affected keys received bursts of denials for a few seconds before automatic reconciliation restored correct balances. Billing pipeline shows duplicate credit reversal events for the same original debit IDs during the shard replay window.
expected_behavior: Shard replay and failover should be idempotent: replaying events must not cause duplicate reversals or double-applies. Balances must stay >= 0 unless customer legitimately consumed more credits.
customer_impact: Some customers experienced brief rate limiting or request denials despite having available credits. No permanent billing discrepancy observed; reconciler fixed balances within minutes. Potential for customer confusion and increased support tickets.
reproduction_steps: Simulate shard move: trigger controlled shard handoff in staging (shard controller scale-down -> scale-up on new node).
Use a high-throughput synthetic client sending requests for a single API key to create a tight burst of debits and ACKs around the handoff window.
Observe ledger events emitted to the debit/reversal stream and measure account balance before, during, and after replay.
Check for duplicate reversal events with identical original_debit_id and mismatched sequence numbers in the event log.
investigation_notes: Initial logs show a pair of reversal events emitted within 200ms for the same debit_id during shard rehydration.

Our fastpath ack handler marks debits as 'committed' and a background reconciler uses 'commit markers' to garbage-collect temporary reservations; during replay both the live handler and the replay path emitted a reversal because the in-memory reservation flag was not yet rehydrated.

Shard replay applies events in timestamp order but there is a race between the event applier and the live message acknowledger when a node accepts traffic while it is still completing state hydration.
Reproducer in staging confirmed that enabling strict traffic quiesce during handoff prevents duplicate reversals.
Telemetry: 87% of incidents clustered around high-churn shards (frequent leader moves) and keys with many concurrent in-flight requests.
root_cause_summary: A race during shard rehydration where incoming live ACKs and the replay applier both processed the same debit lifecycle led to emitting a reversal twice. The ledger subsystem lacked a durable idempotency guard keyed on (debit_id, shard_epoch), so the second reversal was treated as a fresh event and applied, decrementing the balance incorrectly.
mitigation: Short-term: enable aggressive traffic quiescing for shard handoffs (hold new requests until hydration completes) and add a temporary reconciliation window that suppresses enforcement for keys with recent shard transitions. Ops runbook updated. Medium-term: introduce durable idempotency checks in ledger apply (see next steps).
next_steps: Implement durable idempotency store: add a lightweight RocksDB-backed idempotency index per-shard keyed by (debit_id) with a TTL matched to retention window (PR in review: github.com/redwood/ledger/pull/292).
Change apply path to check idempotency index before applying reversals or commits and skip duplicates with logged metrics for duplicate count.
Add unit and integration tests simulating concurrent live-ACK + replay apply with shuffled timing to assert single-apply semantics.
Deploy change behind a feature flag and run canary on low-traffic region for 48h.
Remove temporary traffic quiesce after validation and monitor duplicate-reversal metric underwriting SLA.
Run a one-off reconciler to find accounts that hit negative balance in the last 24h and tag them for customer support outreach if they were rate-limited.
Postmortem and knowledge-share with platform and SRE teams; update design doc at docs/confluence/metering-idempotency.md.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate reversal events for the same debit_id observed in canary for 48h (metric: ledger.duplicate_reversal_count == 0).
No customer-visible rate-limits triggered by negative-balance artifacts in canary region.
Integration tests assert idempotent apply for 10k randomized event orders.
Feature flag rollout completed to 3 regions and reconciler has cleared outstanding negative balance incidents.
